descriptionText:
National Grid is hiring a Graduate Software Technology Engineer to develop, enhance and support digital platforms used in its business operations. The role involves building and maintaining enterprise technology solutions, working with colleagues and stakeholders to deliver improvements, and developing software engineering and automation skills.
Responsibilities
Develop, configure, test and support applications and services across National Grid's enterprise technology platforms
Work with product owners, business analysts, developers and testers to understand business requirements and deliver effective technical solutions
Write secure, well-structured and well-documented code, while building your software engineering and automation skills
Support the testing, deployment and continuous improvement of new features, upgrades and enhancements
Learn how technology products are delivered using industry-standard delivery approaches, including Agile and SAFe methodologies
Collaborate with stakeholders and end users, helping demonstrate new functionality and incorporate feedback into future improvements
Build your technical capability through hands-on delivery, mentoring, training, certifications and exposure to vendor technologies and product roadmaps
Skills
You'll need to achieve a minimum 2:2 in Information Systems/Technology, Computer/Software Science or a closely related degree discipline
It doesn't matter when you graduated or whether you're currently studying towards your qualification
We're looking for graduates who are interested in technology and digital innovation, enjoy solving problems and developing technical solutions, and are keen to build their skills in software development, enterprise platforms and automation
Most importantly, you'll be eager to apply your knowledge in a real-world environment and learn how technology supports business outcomes at scale
National Grid's Early Careers opportunities in the UK are open to all applicants who meet the eligibility criteria including an existing and valid right to work in the UK
Applicants must have the legal right to work in the UK without requiring sponsorship now or in the future under the UK points-based immigration system
Benefits
26 days' annual leave, plus statutory holidays
A competitive pension scheme
Access to flexible benefits, including cycle-to-work and holiday buy/sell schemes
The opportunity to participate in our Sharesave and Share Incentive Plans
A £2,000 joining bonus upon starting the programme
A £2,400 payment upon successful completion of the programme
An accommodation allowance of up to £200 per month as you move around the business during placements
Additional annual leave when moving between placements, plus support with relocating your personal belongings
Dedicated mentoring, regular feedback, networking opportunities, and volunteering opportunities to support your development
A permanent role with National Grid upon successful completion of the programme
Flexible hybrid working, where possible
Tailored development programme
In-person and virtual development sessions throughout the programme
Access to 1:1 coaching and a mentor from a previous cohort
Company Overview
National Grid facilitates electricity and gas transmission system and focuses on delivering clean energy. It was founded in 1990, and is headquartered in London, England, GBR, with a workforce of 10001+ employees. Its website is https://www.nationalgrid.com.
